newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu backs multinational force for Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu backs multinational force for Zaire.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko supports proposals for a multinational force to get relief to refugees in his country and help them return home, a U.N. envoy said after meeting him on Wednesday.

Envoy Raymond Chretien quoted Mobutu as saying he would do his utmost so that a unilateral ceasefire declared by Tutsi rebels fighting Zairean forces could hold in order to let the multinational force work.

"President Mobutu told me Zaire would do everything possible to maintain this period of calm so that the multinational force discussed in Nairobi may be able to rapidly allow for food to reach refugees and help them return to their home countries, including of course Rwanda," Chretien said.
"He was very clear, very categorical," Chretien told reporters after the half-hour meeting at Mobutu's French Riviera villa.

An eight-nation African summit in Nairobi on Tuesday called on the United Nations to send a "neutral" protection force to create havens from which refugees could go home along safe corridors. But volunteers for the force appeared sparse.

France, Spain and Ethiopia have offered troops for the force initially proposed by France. Paris has said it wanted all major countries to participate and the force should be rapidly replaced by African troops.
French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette voiced disappointment at the lack of response, blaming it on "the international community's spinelessness".
"I'm knocking on doors, asking if anyone is prepared to assume his responsibilities. The answer is 'Could you come back tomorrow?" de Charette told LCI television.
Chretien, Canada's ambassador to the United States, planned to fly later to Kinshasa for talks with Zairean prime minister Kendo wa Dondo.
The 66-year-old Zairean president, who has been away from Zaire since August undergoing treatment for prostate cancer, earlier made a brief appearance before a handful of reporters.
Wearing an elegant black and white jacket, he briefly chatted with a French TF1 television crew. TF1 said Mobutu looked tired but his voice was well assured.
Zairean ambassador to France Baya Ramazini said Mobutu was getting better and would soon return home.
"The president will go back home in the next few days. The situation demands it," he told the reporters invited in to the villa to see Mobutu.
In Kinshasa, Mobutu spokesman Samba Kabuya Lumuna said the president would be home in a few days, but added: "No one knows exactly when".
Mobutu underwent surgery for his cancer in Switzerland. He left Lausanne for his sprawling luxury pink and white marble villa near Nice on Monday.
He has remained silent since fighting broke out in his country, trapping more than one million starving refugees and threatening the government's hold on northeastern Zaire.
"The president is getting much better but he is still convalescing and has resumed a bit of activity in light of the situation in his country," Ramazini said.
He said Mobutu was following developments back in Zaire through regular contacts with senior government officials including Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo.
All government actions were taken in agreement with the president, he said.

Chretien told reporters on his arrival at Nice airport late on Tuesday night that Mobutu had been the "guarantor of the security of his country for many decades...He has been an active president who was always in control when he was in Kinshasa".
